Previous results from the HYPerluminous quasars at the Epoch of ReionizatION (HYPERION) sample of $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs, powered by the most rapidly accreted SMBHs, suggested a link between X-ray spectral slope and long-term growth efficiency. We test whether the steep X-ray spectra of luminous z>6 QSOs are a general property of early SMBH growth or a peculiarity of the most efficiently grown SMBHs, using a sample extended mainly to the lowest growth efficiencies. We analysed the largest and most X-ray sensitive sample of 28 luminous QSOs at $z \simeq 5.85-7.56$ (26 used in the correlation analysis), combining HYPERION targets, luminous non-HYPERION sources, and QSOs powered by moderately accreting SMBHs newly observed in our XMM-Newton Large Programme. We re-derived black hole masses and growth indicators for the entire sample homogeneously, incorporating the latest JWST-based spectroscopic measurements to ensure the most consistent and high-quality characterization across all targets. We found no statistically significant correlation between coronal spectral parameters and BH growth indicators: luminous $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs systematically show steep X-ray continua, with high photon indices and/or low high-energy cutoffs, consistent with cold coronae, possibly linked to rapid accretion. Finally, if steep X-ray slopes are common among early AGN, they may significantly reduce count rates, at fixed intrinsic luminosity, in future surveys of the EoR, affecting the detectability of steep-spectrum X-ray sources and thus the census of the early AGN population.

papers.title_en: Optical Signatures of Black Holes Surrounded by a Generalized Cloud of Strings
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we investigate the optical signatures of black holes surrounded by a generalized cloud of strings, described by the Letelier--Alencar spacetime. We first analyze null geodesics, showing that the string parameters can either increase or decrease the photon sphere radius and the critical impact parameter relative to their Schwarzschild values. Since the spacetime is not asymptotically flat, the critical impact parameter does not directly coincide with the physical shadow radius. We use this distinction to derive constraints on the model parameters from the shadow radius bounds of Sgr A* and M87*. In the weak-field regime, we calculate the light deflection angle using both the Gauss--Bonnet method and a perturbative expansion of the null geodesic equations, obtaining consistent results that contain a contribution from the asymptotically conical geometry in addition to the local gravitational deflection. We also examine the Shapiro time delay and identify a distance dependent contribution associated with the non Minkowskian asymptotic background. Finally, we study the optical appearance of geometrically and optically thin accretion disks and construct celestial sphere images through backward ray tracing. The transfer functions and lensing images show that the generalized cloud of strings modifies the null geodesic mapping in a nonuniform manner rather than producing a simple rescaling of the Schwarzschild image. In particular, configurations with a smaller shadow may still produce an outward displacement of the main Einstein ring image, demonstrating that different optical observables probe distinct aspects of photon propagation in this geometry.

papers.title_en: Superconductivity in a Two-Orbital Hatsugai-Kohmoto Model at Half Filling
papers.abstract_en: Multiband superconductivity gives rise to a rich landscape of possible pairing states. Here we study superconductivity emerging from a half-filled normal state in a two-orbital extension of the Hatsugai-Kohmoto model, an exactly solvable model of correlated electrons with momentum-local interactions, which provides a minimal framework to explore the interplay of strong correlations, orbital structure and pairing symmetry. For a system with point-group symmetry $\rm D_{4h}$, we classify the symmetry-allowed superconducting gap structures, taking into account spin, orbital and momentum degrees of freedom. We further compute the critical temperature and the superconducting order parameter for selected pairing channels as functions of interaction and pairing strength within a mean-field treatment. Our results provide a systematic framework for analyzing superconductivity in the orbital Hatsugai-Kohmoto model and extend symmetry-based approaches to correlated multiband settings.

papers.title_en: Electric and Heat Transport in One-Dimensional SNS Junctions with Energy-Dependent Transmission
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the phase-independent dc components of the electric and heat currents through a one-dimensional superconductor-normal-metal-superconductor (SNS) junction subject to chemical-potential and temperature differences between two superconducting reservoirs. Using a scattering approach based on the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations, we incorporate multiple Andreev reflections while retaining the energy dependence of transmission through the normal region. We compare energy-independent, quantum-dot-type, and quantum-point-contact transmission profiles. At low bias, both currents exhibit nonlinear features associated with the superconducting gap and multiple Andreev reflections. Their responses to a temperature difference depend remarkably on the transmission profile. At a small finite bias, the electric current depends weakly on the temperature difference for the energy-independent and quantum-dot-type profiles, whereas the quantum-point-contact profile produces a pronounced nonlinear response. The heat current depends nonlinearly on the temperature difference for all three profiles over the parameter range investigated. These results highlight the role of the transmission profile in nonlinear electric and heat transport through SNS junctions and provide a microscopic reference for related transport studies in mesoscopic fermionic superfluid junctions.

papers.title_en: Nonreciprocal black holes with primary hair in beyond Horndeski gravity: Exact solutions and stability
papers.abstract_en: We develop a novel systematic method for constructing exact, static, and asymptotically flat black-hole solutions in shift-symmetric and $Z_2$-symmetric beyond Horndeski theories. In contrast to previous studies, our approach does not rely on the restrictive reciprocal condition $g_{tt}g_{rr}=-1$, allowing for more general geometries characterized by two independent metric functions. The resulting solution space contains two qualitatively distinct types of hair originating from different branches of the theory. One branch is characterized by khronometric hair, while the other by genuine scalar hair. In both, the scalar profile defines a nontrivial preferred foliation, but the shift-symmetry Noether current and the associated propagating degree of freedom are trivial for the former and nonvanishing for the latter. Focusing mainly on the second branch, we derive several distinct families of exact black-hole solutions. In general, these solutions are singular and exhibit primary scalar hair associated with an independent scalar charge. Nevertheless, we demonstrate that they can be regularized to yield regular black-hole or solitonic configurations, for which the scalar hair becomes secondary. We further investigate the stability properties of these solutions under linear perturbations by analyzing the axial sector and the monopole $(\ell=0)$ mode of the even-parity sector. For representative solutions with scalar hair, the perturbative analysis provides evidence for linear stability under the modes considered.

papers.title_en: Effect of ultralight dark matter on compact binary mergers
papers.abstract_en: The growing catalogue of gravitational wave events enables a statistical analysis of compact binary mergers, typically quantified by the binary merger rate density. This quantity can be influenced by ambient factors, following which, in this work we have investigated the impact of dark matter environment on the merger statistics. We construct a baseline astrophysical model of eccentric and quasi-circular compact binary mergers and extend it by incorporating a model of ultra light dark matter, which affects the orbital evolution of binaries through accretion and dynamical friction. Our analysis of the merged population of binary progenitors demonstrates that, compared to the baseline model, ULDM can potentially alter the merger statistics around an optimal combination of ambient density $\lesssim10^4 \textrm{GeV}/\textrm{cm}^{3}$ and eccentricity $\sim 0.5$. A comparison with the gravitational wave data from the GWTC-3 catalogue provides crucial insight into potential observational signatures of the ULDM in merger events, leading to possible constraints on the existence and density of dark matter distribution in galaxies.

papers.title_en: Note on arithmetic structure of modulus vacua in flux compactifications
papers.abstract_en: We study modulus stabilization by background fluxes. Within the truncated complex-structure sector, the F-term conditions of the complex structure moduli are described by a holomorphic quadratic equation. As concrete examples, we consider the $T^6/(\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2')$ orientifold model and a simple Calabi-Yau compactification. The modulus values show specific patterns. For example, they exhibit a structure related to the Farey sequence. The void structure appears around modulus vacua with high degeneracies. We find a correlation between the degeneracy and the void area. The modulus vacua are related by discrete Abelian symmetries generated by the Gauss composition law, which includes the CP symmetry. Spontaneous CP violation is also discussed.

papers.title_en: Mode-selective electron-phonon coupling drives charge density waves in the kagome metals YRu$_3$Si$_2$ and LaRu$_3$Si$_2$
papers.abstract_en: YRu$_3$Si$_2$ and LaRu$_3$Si$_2$ host the highest charge density wave (CDW) transition temperatures ever reported in kagome metals, $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}\approx 800$ and 400~K, with propagation vectors $Q_{\mathrm{CDW}}\approx(1/2,0,0)$ and $(1/4,0,0)$, respectively. The microscopic mechanism behind these record values has remained unresolved. Here, we combine anharmonic phonon renormalization extracted from molecular dynamics driven by a machine-learned force field with mode-resolved electron-phonon coupling (EPC) analysis to identify this mechanism. The CDW is driven by mode-selective EPC: the Ru out-of-plane phonon modes couple the Ru-$d_{xz}/d_{yz}$ and Si-$p_x/p_y$ orbitals, and the phonon linewidth peaks sharply at $Q_{\mathrm{CDW}}$, while the featureless electronic susceptibility rules out Fermi-surface nesting. Phonon anharmonicity melts the CDW, and the anharmonic phonon spectra reproduce both $Q_{\mathrm{CDW}}$ and $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}$ in good agreement with experiments. Molecular dynamics simulations also visualize the CDW melting in real space. Chemical bonding analysis further shows that the smaller Y$^{3+}$ radius strengthens the Ru-Ru bonds, enhancing lattice rigidity and accounting for the factor-of-two higher $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}$ of YRu$_3$Si$_2$. Our results establish a unified microscopic picture of CDW formation and melting in kagome metals YRu$_3$Si$_2$ and LaRu$_3$Si$_2$.

papers.title_en: Maximal Total Quantum Dimension at Bounded Rank in WZW Modular Tensor Categories
papers.abstract_en: We determine the maximal torus topological entanglement entropy (TEE) at bounded torus ground-state degeneracy within simply connected untwisted Wess--Zumino--Witten theories. For a fixed modular tensor category $\mathcal C$, maximization over normalized torus ground states gives $\max_ψΓ_{T^2}(ψ)=2\log{\mathcal D(\mathcal C)}$, attained in particular by the vacuum-flux state. The remaining problem is therefore to maximize total $\mathcal D$ at bounded categorical rank. For a simple WZW category $\mathcal C(\mathfrak g,k)$, write $r(\mathfrak g,k)$ and $\mathcal D(\mathfrak g,k)$ for its categorical rank and total quantum dimension, and define $F_{\WZW}(R)=\sup_{r(\mathfrak g,k)\leq R}2\log\mathcal D(\mathfrak g,k)$. We prove the sharp asymptotic law $\lim_{R\to\infty}\frac{F_{\WZW}(R)}{(\log_2R)^2} =\frac{7ζ(3)}{4π^2}.$ The balanced symplectic sequence $Sp(2n)_n$ attains the coefficient. The constant arises from the odd Fourier modes of the type-$C$ root product at equal rank and level. A sharp entropy--spectral inequality, rank-level duality, and fixed-rank estimates give the global upper bound. A separate corollary extends the same leading law to semisimple WZW categories,equivalently finite Deligne products of simple factors. The unrestricted TQFT envelope remains open; the theorem is sharp within the stated WZW class and supplies a constructive lower bound for the general problem.

papers.title_en: Nonradial perturbations of static charged wormholes
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the nonradial quasinormal-mode spectrum of static charged Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes in Einstein--Maxwell theory minimally coupled to a phantom scalar field. The background solutions are known in closed form and comprise three classes: subcritical, critical and supercritical, which all approach the extremal Reissner--Nordström geometry at the boundary of their domain of existence. We derive the linear perturbation equations for axial and polar sectors, including the coupled gravitational, electromagnetic and phantom-scalar degrees of freedom, and compute the corresponding spectra by means of a Chebyshev spectral method. The uncharged limit reproduces the known Ellis--Bronnikov spectrum and exhibits the expected electromagnetic isospectrality. For charged configurations we track the axial and polar branches across the three families of solutions and identify the effect of the charge on the damping times and oscillation frequencies. In particular, we find that charge can substantially reduce damping rates as the extremal Reissner--Nordström limit is approached. We also uncover a nonradial polar instability, most clearly visible in the fundamental $l=2$ branch for sufficiently large wormhole masses. This instability is distinct from the familiar radial Ellis--Bronnikov instability and shows that the nonradial sector imposes additional constraints on the dynamical viability of charged wormholes.

papers.title_en: Renormalization, cutoff, and gluing for a quartic model with boundary
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we study the renormalization of a three-dimensional quartic model on a compact connected Riemannian manifold with a boundary. We show that, in addition to the standard shift of the mass parameter, it is necessary to take into account boundary contributions involving singular coefficients. This indicates the need to extend the classical action within the framework of standard renormalization theory. The requirements of consistency regarding the gluing of manifolds lead to renormalization of an operator on the boundary.

papers.title_en: Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains
papers.abstract_en: We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1} \times S^2$, where $M_{1,1}$ is two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and $S^2$ is the two-sphere. We investigate scalar-field dynamics and the fate of the Aretakis instability. Although Aretakis-like modes arise in a local analysis of the throat, they do not lead to a physical instability of the mimicker. A scalar perturbation initially localized in the throat gives rise, at late times, to a sequence of signals with a characteristic separation $t_{\rm delay}\sim 1/λ$, where $λ\ll 1$ is a deformation parameter. This timescale is parametrically larger than the echo time $t_{\rm echo}\sim \ln(1/λ)$ characteristic of non-extremal black-hole mimickers. We refer to this sequence as a {\it long-delay signal train}. Geometrically, the periodicity of the long-delay signals is associated with periodic geodesics on $S^2$. We then extend the construction to extremal Kerr. In this case, the throat region approaches a generalized product geometry involving $M_{1,1}$ and a two-dimensional surface $Σ_2$. The corresponding signals are expected to form a quasi-periodic signal train, reflecting the quasi-periodic geodesic motion on $Σ_2$. We also comment on the generalization to wormhole mimickers of non-extremal black holes and on the implications of these results for unitarity in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence.

papers.title_en: Convergence of Roberts flow dynamos in Eulerian and Lagrangian codes
papers.abstract_en: Standard benchmark tests for numerical magnetohydrodynamics codes focus on one- and two-dimensional problems that ignore the possibility of dynamos, i.e., an exponential instability converting kinetic energy into magnetic energy. They also tend to ignore magnetic helicity conservation that can have dramatic effects in periodic domains. The existence of magnetic diffusion is crucial for dynamos, as was exemplified by the impossibility of finding dynamo solutions when using Euler potentials, which is a perfectly valid approach in the absence of magnetic diffusion. The Roberts flows~I, II, III, and IV are two-dimensional flows that support three-dimensional dynamos, all of which are also large-scale dynamos in the sense that their planar averages are of significant strengths, even though flow~II is pointwise non-helical. Here we demonstrate the numerical convergence properties of solutions obtained using discretisation schemes of second, sixth, and tenth order in the mesh width in the Pencil Code, compare the results with the SPH-based SWIFT code, and present a list of averaged quantities that facilitate their use in characterising the solutions as benchmarks. In addition, we present a procedure to obtain two-dimensional time-independent magnetic field visualisation for all Roberts flows, and perform per-pixel comparison between the Pencil and SWIFT codes. The rich combination of features makes Roberts flows an excellent dynamo benchmark for the direct numerical simulations of magnetohydrodynamics equations.

papers.title_en: Linearised gravity as edge modes & manifest duality and Lorentz covariance
papers.abstract_en: We present the first formulation of linearised gravity in four dimensions which is manifestly Lorentz covariant and democratic, i.e. treats the two frames related by electric-magnetic duality on equal footing. It is well-known that four-dimensional linearised gravity belongs to a class of singleton representations of the four-dimensional conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$. Our key insight is viewing this algebra as the isometry of $\text{AdS}_5$ and realising the massless spin-2 field as edge modes of a five-dimensional topological field taking values in a specific finite-dimensional representation of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$. The desired four-dimensional action is then found by a covariant boundary reduction procedure.

papers.title_en: Beyond the Dolgov-Kawasaki instability: Covariant scalaron stability, entropy transport, and inner horizons in f(R) gravity
papers.abstract_en: The Dolgov-Kawasaki instability tests the local scalaron response in metric $f(R)$ gravity, but does not determine strong-field horizon dynamics. We separate these questions using $F=f_R$ and the Legendre potential $\mathcal U(F)=FR-f$. The scalaron restoring coefficient is $m_{\rm sc}^2=(F-Rf_{RR})/(3f_{RR})$, whereas exact spherical Wald-area transport identities cancel the scalaron Hessian. Their Einstein-frame interpretation distinguishes longitudinal kinetic focusing from potential-dependent cross-focusing. We prove that, at fixed constant-curvature background with tracefree matter, transport depends only on $(f,f_R)$, while the scalaron mass depends on the independently adjustable $f_{RR}$. Reissner-Nordström in $f(R)=R+αR^2$ gives an exact discriminator: identical background transport coexists with opposite scalaron mass signs. A charged solution with varying $F$ and a cosmological check test the identities beyond this constant-$F$ sector. For a nonzero massive scalaron tail transmitted to a nondegenerate Cauchy horizon, a conditional fixed-background estimate gives a nonintegrable contribution to generalized entropy focusing. This estimate does not establish nonlinear mass inflation or a particular extendibility class. The results provide a layered framework for coupling regularity, background transport, scalaron stability, and nonlinear inner-horizon evolution.

papers.title_en: Dielectric constant of holographic insulator from quantum geometry
papers.abstract_en: We study dielectric properties of holographic insulators from the quantum geometry of the ground state. We realize the insulating state by the pseudoscalar interaction of holographic fermions and calculate the fermionic Green function to extract the effective hamiltonian. We then derive the quantum metric and Berry curvature to compute the transports and finally get the dielectric constant from the imaginary part of conductivity.

papers.title_en: Spin-outcome correlations and memory-assisted entropic uncertainty in Bhabha scattering with an entangled spectator
papers.abstract_en: We investigate spin-outcome correlations and memory-assisted entropic uncertainty in tree-level Bhabha scattering, where an incident electron $A$ scatters with a positron $B$ initially entangled with a spectator electron $C$. For the fixed-angle post-selected final state, we compare the total memory-assisted uncertainty $U_A$ for three alternative Pauli measurements on $A$ with the entanglement entropy $S(ρ_A)$ across the $A|BC$ partition. We resolve $U_A$ into the separate uncertainties $U_B$ and $U_C$ and evaluate the corresponding outcome-memory mutual-information sums $G_B$ and $G_C$. This separates changes in the randomness of the outcomes on $A$ from changes in their correlations with each memory. In the parameter regions studied, enhanced $A|BC$ entanglement is accompanied by lower $U_A$, most prominently near high-energy backscattering. An analytic treatment of this limit shows that $B$ factorizes from $AC$: $G_B$ vanishes, whereas $G_C$ increases with the initial $B$-$C$ entanglement. An entropic complete complementarity analysis characterizes the accompanying loss of local helicity predictability in $ρ_A$ and changes in the coherence, predictability, and mixedness of the interacting pair $ρ_{AB}$. These results show that initial $B$-$C$ entanglement can lower the total memory-assisted uncertainty in high-energy backscattering by strengthening spin-outcome correlations with the spectator $C$, thereby identifying the distinct roles of the interacting particle and the spectator as quantum memories.

papers.title_en: FLRW-Compatible Tensors and Perfect-Fluid Universality in Modified Gravity
papers.abstract_en: We study FLRW-compatible tensor fields on Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker spacetimes in $(D+1)$ dimensions equipped with Levi-Civita connection. We prove that any covariant rank-$N$ tensor field invariant under the spatial homogeneity and isotropy group, with $D>N$, admits a finite decomposition into monomials constructed from the metric tensor $g_{μν}$ and the unit timelike vector $u_μ$, with scalar coefficients depending only on cosmic time. As a direct consequence, any rank-two correction term appearing in an Einstein-like rearrangement of the FLRW background field equations has the effective perfect-fluid form for $D>2$. Thus, the result provides an arbitrary-rank tensorial classification underlying the perfect-fluid structure of modified gravity equations on FLRW backgrounds, complementing existing rank-two universality results. Applications to generalized Friedmann equations and to the geodesic deviation equation in modified gravity are also discussed.

papers.title_en: No Particle Production and Integrability in AdS$_2$
papers.abstract_en: We propose an analogue of the no particle production condition in two-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, and demonstrate how this criterion uniquely reconstructs the curved-space Liouville and Toda theories via general-multiplicity holographic correlators.

papers.title_en: Data augmentation by an electro-vibratory feedback improves signal interpretation by neural networks
papers.abstract_en: Data-driven machine learning algorithms represent an alternative to numerical or analytical modeling of vibrating objects for the purpose of extracting their material or geometric properties. Their performance is conditioned by the quality of the training dataset, which should contain all possible production configurations of the object and measurement conditions. In this work, we propose a data-augmentation method based on manipulations of the vibration properties rather than numerical signal post-processing. Instead of modifying the sample’s material or geometry, we connect an additional sensor and actuator to the sample and use low-latency electronics to control the feedback signal. This delivers an electromechanical system with tunable oscillation properties. This signal diversification method is demonstrated on the classification of correct and incorrect adhesion of two aluminum plates. The labeling accuracy of 67% on nine unknown test objects, when trained on a single unchangeable training object, increases to 83% when the variety of the training vibration signals is augmented by varying the parameters of the electrovibratory feedback. This provides advantages for industrial quality control, where a large number of reference training samples are not available.

papers.title_en: u-d Quark Matter in the Enhanced pQCD Model and u-d Quark Stars in Gravity’s Rainbow
The Search for Mev-scale Neutrinos in Temporal Coincidence With o4 Gravitational Wave Events Using the Sno+ Experiment
papers.abstract_en: This dissertation presents a search for low-energy neutrinos in temporal coincidence with gravitational wave events reported by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration during the fourth observing run (O4), using 499.0 days of data collected during the liquid scintillator phase of the SNO+ experiment. The search uses inverse beta decay (IBD), which is primarily sensitive to electron antineutrinos, and neutrino-proton elastic scattering, a complementary neutral current channel providing sensitivity to all neutrino flavors. Candidate events were identified using optimized reconstruction and event-selection criteria developed with Monte Carlo simulations and validated with background-only data. The IBD background rate was measured directly from data, naturally incorporating reactor antineutrinos, geoneutrinos, radioactive backgrounds, cosmogenic backgrounds, and accidental coincidences present during detector operation. A model-independent framework was developed using flat spectrum neutrino Monte Carlo samples, allowing the detector response to be evaluated as a function of neutrino energy and applied to different theoretical emission models. As part of this work, improvements were made to the SNO+ Monte Carlo simulation, including modifications to the IBD generator to produce a true flat neutrino spectrum and corrections to the implementation of the neutrino-proton elastic scattering cross section. Detector characterization studies, including measurements of the deployed scintillator light yield and investigations of detector timing and electronics performance, were also performed to validate the detector response used throughout the analysis. The final gravitational wave-coincident dataset contained 143 candidates overlapping stable SNO+ data-taking periods. After excluding candidates classified as terrestrial or unknown by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration, the final astrophysical sample used for compact binary merger fluence limits contained 126 gravitational wave candidates. No statistically significant neutrino excess was observed in either the IBD or neutrino-proton elastic scattering channels. The IBD search observed no coincident candidates in the final astrophysical gravitational wave sample, consistent with an expected background of 1.25 ± 0.09 events. The corresponding Feldman-Cousins 90% confidence level upper limit is N90stack = 1.47 signal events. Stacked average (per gravitational wave) upper limits on the electron antineutrino fluence were derived for both monoenergetic neutrino emission and model-dependent spectra, including thermal neutrino and core-collapse supernova-inspired models used as detector sensitivity benchmarks. The neutrino-proton elastic scattering search represents the first application of this all-flavor channel to a gravitational wave-coincident neutrino search. Using an optimized ±50 s coincidence window, 108424 candidate events were observed, consistent with the expected background of 108345 ± 786 events estimated from local sidebands. The observed 0.24σ fluctuation is consistent with the background-only hypothesis. For the final astrophysical gravitational wave sample, the Feldman-Cousins method gives a 90% confidence level upper limit of N90stack = 1479.6 signal events. These results are used to derive the first all-flavor neutrino-proton elastic scattering fluence limits associated with compact binary merger candidates. The resulting SNO+ IBD fluence limits improve upon previous liquid scintillator gravitational wave-neutrino searches by approximately an order of magnitude in the few-MeV energy region, primarily due to the larger fiducial target mass, increased gravitational wave sample size, and low background rate achieved in SNO+. The neutrino-proton elastic scattering results establish the first all-flavor MeV neutrino search through this interaction channel in coincidence with gravitational wave events. Together, these analyses extend previous multi-messenger searches performed by Borexino, KamLAND, and Super-Kamiokande and demonstrate the capability of SNO+ to search for weak neutrino signals associated with astrophysical transients.

papers.title_en: Quantum Key Distribution Network Simulator With Hyperparameter Tuning for Realistic Performance Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Realistic simulation of quantum key distribution (QKD) networks requires a combination of precise models of quantum channels and network functions. Unfortunately, existing QKD network simulators lack either rigorous quantum physics modeling or network key-management and routing protocols, which limit their practical applicability. To address this limitation, we propose a QKD network simulator with hyperparameter tuning (QKDSim-HT), a NetSquid-based simulator specialized for polarization-based discrete-variable QKD networks. Specifically, QKDSim-HT models properties in quantum physics (photon loss, polarization-dependent depolarization, detector inefficiencies, dark counts, and dead times) as well as advanced functionalities in networking algorithms (multi-hop key relay and adaptive routing). Extensive simulations over diverse topologies reveal that the networking performance varied with respect to the fundamental properties of quantum physics, such as depolarization, fiber length, and channel attenuation. As a representative use case of QKDSim-HT, simulation results from QKDSim-HT over simple examples clearly manifest that a design of QKD networks highly affects performance of the networks. Accordingly, QKDSim-HT can serve as a practical platform for performance evaluation and optimization of quantum secured network.

papers.title_en: Suppression of two-stream and Weibel instabilities in ultra-relativistic electron–positron plasma
papers.abstract_en: We present a unified theoretical framework for analyzing both electrostatic two-stream and electromagnetic Weibel instabilities in counterstreaming electron-positron pair plasmas. Through systematic derivation of dispersion relations in non-relativistic and relativistic regimes, we demonstrate how the symmetric mass ratio fundamentally alters instability characteristics compared to electron-ion systems. The two-stream instability, driven by longitudinal electrostatic perturbations parallel to beam motion, exhibits enhanced growth rates in pair plasmas due to equal contributions from both species, with relativistic suppression scaling as γ0−3 for both electrons and positrons. The Weibel instability, arising from transverse electromagnetic modes perpendicular to streaming directions, lacks the heavy-ion stabilization present in electron-ion plasmas, producing broader unstable spectral ranges and modified saturation levels. We derive explicit conditions determining the relative dominance of each mechanism across parameter space defined by drift velocity, wavenumber orientation, and relativistic Lorentz factor. Our analysis shows that longitudinal two-stream modes dominate at small perpendicular wavenumbers and moderate drift velocities, while transverse Weibel modes become prevalent at high perpendicular wavenumbers and large velocity spreads or temperature anisotropies. These findings have direct implications for understanding magnetic field generation, particle acceleration, and energy dissipation in astrophysical pair plasmas including pulsar wind nebulae, gamma-ray burst internal shocks, and active galactic nuclei jets where counterstreaming pair populations naturally arise.

papers.title_en: Developing and validating models of open quantum systems in solid-state nanostructures
papers.abstract_en: Realistic quantum devices are open systems, and their behaviour depends not only on the subsystem of interest but also on how the environment is modelled and how the relevant observables are extracted. This thesis studies that problem in three settings. First, we study cavity-assisted qubit readout beyond the dispersive regime. We show that once coherent excitation exchange and dissipation become relevant, a microscopic treatment is needed to describe the readout quantitatively, and the optimal readout is set by a trade-off between signal accumulation and the distinguishability of the readout states. Second, we compare fermionic and spin baths in non-interacting transport models and show that spin baths reproduce fermionic reduced dynamics only in the large-bath weak-coupling limit, while clear deviations appear for smaller baths and near half-filling. Third, we study charge transport in molecular junctions using Automated Compression of Environments (ACE). There, the main difficulty is not the time evolution itself, but the extraction of the transport current, since this observable depends on system-environment correlations and is therefore not contained in the reduced system density matrix alone. We show that a probe-mode construction provides a viable route to reformulate the current as a system observable. This thesis advances our understanding of what is required for accurate modelling of open quantum dynamics across a range of solid-state settings, from cavity-assisted qubit readout to charge transport in molecular junctions.

papers.title_en: Using Printed Circuit Boards and MOSFET Switch Arrays Toward the Reliable Manufacture of Superconducting Rectifiers
papers.abstract_en: Using superconducting rectifiers to energize high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets is a promising approach to accelerate the uptake of HTS magnet technology. In this work, we start to address two limitations of the HTS superconducting rectifier concepts published to date; their low magnet charging voltages, and the variable properties of their HTS-based switches. Our approach is to test a centre-tapped full-wave transformer–rectifier utilizing HTS secondary windings and switch-arrays of Si <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small>s mounted on a printed-circuit board (PCB). This approach has the advantage of greatly facilitating reproducible and reliable manufacture. The rectifier demonstrated magnet charging voltages exceeding a cycle-averaged 80 mV at 100 A and with typically more than 30% of the power supplied to the primary coils delivered to the magnet. We found it to be resilient to our preliminary thermal-cycling testing, with no degradation in performance observed over eight liquid-nitrogen to ambient (77–295 K) thermal cycles. We compare the impact of voltage- and current-controlled modes for the rectifier’s power supply. Our conclusion is that superconducting rectifiers using <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small> switch arrays placed on PCBs is a very promising approach for low-current HTS magnet power supplies.

papers.title_en: Compact High Turns Ratio Superconducting Transformer: Comparison Between Cu and REBCO Winding Materials
papers.abstract_en: Compact high turns ratio superconducting transformers are used to transfer power between low-current copper/ semiconductor-based circuits and high-current superconductor-based circuits. This type of transformer is a key component in devices, such as superconducting transformer rectifiers and superconducting current source inverters. Typically the copper winding and the superconducting winding are arranged with a turn ratio above 100:1, respectively, and are situated entirely within a cryogenic environment. The ohmic losses associated with the high count copper winding is problematic for most cryogenic applications and demands attention even when low currents on the order of 1–10 A are used. To address this problem, a transformer has been made using rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) high-temperature superconductor (HTS) coated conductor for both the primary and secondary windings. The coupling coefficient and power consumption of this transformer were measured and compared to an equivalent transformer consisting of a copper primary winding and HTS secondary winding. The HTS primary was found to provide a significant reduction in transformer power consumption and a slight improvement to transformer coupling at frequencies below <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. An increased transformer core loss and winding AC loss began to negate these efficiency improvements above <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. In addition, cowinding the primary and secondary windings provided a higher coupling coefficient and lower power consumption for all winding combinations and frequencies tested. Finally, a short discussion on the implications of these findings respect to superconducting transformer rectifiers contextualizes the findings.

papers.title_en: The Primary Interaction Compton Couple algorithm for sorting GRETINA/GRETA interaction points
Alfvénicity and proximity to parallel-mode marginal stability in the slow solar wind
Mechanical Characteristics of Aluminium-Stabilized Stacked REBCO Tape Cable for the CEPC Detector Magnet
papers.abstract_en: This article investigates the mechanical characteristics and critical current performance of aluminum-stabilized stacked REBCO tape cable (ASTC) for the circular electron-positron collider detector magnet. In-plane bending, torsion, and uniaxial tension tests are carried out, combined by finite element analysis. The correlation between critical current and strain under different loading conditions is systematically analyzed, and key mechanical thresholds are determined. Results show that the minimum allowable in-plane bending diameter is 1200 mm. The critical twist pitch is 327 mm. The critical current degrades to 95% of the initial value when the tensile strain in the REBCO tape reaches 0.37%. This study provides essential experimental data and theoretical support for the structural design and engineering application of ASTC in high-field superconducting magnets.

papers.title_en: Designing Josephson Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers: EM-Circuit Cosimulation and Experimental Validation
papers.abstract_en: The development of large-scale superconducting quantum computers critically depends on the accurate readout of qubit states. To enable this, cryogenic parametric amplifiers have been proposed and developed, and have since found widespread use in small-signal detection applications. Among various amplifier architectures, Josephson traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) are widely adopted due to their broad bandwidth, high saturation power, and compatibility with superconducting qubits. In this work, we present a design workflow of JTWPAs based on a cosimulation approach combining electromagnetic (EM) and circuit-level simulation. We apply this method to a uniform JTWPA, comparing our simulation results with experimental data. To mitigate the challenge of constructing lumped-element circuit models usually used in the conventional simulation method, we directly perform full EM analysis of the device to accurately determine its linear response. The extracted S-parameters are then fed into a nonlinear harmonic balance simulator with Josephson junctions modeled as circuit elements. By doing so, the linear and gain properties of the JTWPA are extracted. Different factors that impact device performance including gain compression, phase matching, and fabrication imperfections are further investigated and modeled. A good agreement between simulation and measurements is identified, establishing the effectiveness of our approach in designing quantum parametric amplifiers.

papers.title_en: Mathematics of effective q-plate in polarization optics
papers.abstract_en: The q-plate is a spatially inhomogeneous SU(2) birefringent optical element that has garnered significant interest due to its ability to mediate the spin-orbit interaction of light and facilitate the generation of structured light with singularities. The q-plate features a spatially varying fast axis orientation defined by three parameters: the topological charge q, retardance delta, and the offset angle $alpha_0$. While the parameter alpha_0 can be changed many times by rotation, any change in the charge and/or retardance entails the fabrication of a new plate. This limitation can be overcome through the concept of an effective waveplate, where multiple waveplates, homogeneous or inhomogeneous, are aligned coaxially so that, under specific constraints, the composite system emulates the behavior of a single effective waveplate. This work presents a comprehensive mathematical formalism for realizing an effective waveplate through a cascaded configuration of three q-plates, each chosen as either a quarter-wave q-plate, a half-wave q-plate, or a combination thereof. Some configurations offer tunability of the retardance over the full range from 0 to $2pi$, even though q-plates with fixed retardances of $pi/2$ and pi are used in sequence to form an effective q-plate. This feature enables holonomic polarization walk on the higher-order Poincare sphere. Such a capability holds significant potential for applications involving structured light associated with the higher-order Poincare sphere, particularly in controlled polarization transformations and polarization-topology engineering.

papers.title_en: Bayesian vs Deep learning: Parameter constraints for an anisotropic universe in f(Q) gravity
Quantum Key Distribution Based Physical Layer Security Applied in Complex Modulation Formats for Optical Fiber Links
papers.abstract_en: A Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) based Physical Layer Security (PLS) scheme (QKD-PLS) for optical fiber links is proposed and evaluated. In detail, a novel amplitude and phase scrambling technique for exploiting and seamlessly integrating high key rate QKD for the encryption of the modulation parameters of conventional complex modulation schemes like M-ary Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (M-QAM) and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is described. Scrambling is applied to both preamble (pilot signals) and payload segments of the transmission frame, to prevent the eavesdroppers from performing vital receiver functionalities such as frame synchronization and channel estimation. Additionally, a practical Key Management System (KMS) taking care of all key synchronization processes is developed and introduced. Moreover, another advantage of QKD exploitation to the proposed solution comes from the application of high entropy kbps-rate QKD keys feeding pseudo-random number generators, to modify the broadband modulation symbols in one-time pad, therefore significantly improving data protection. Experimental evaluation via a transmission scenario in fiber links is also presented, depicting the efficacy of the QKD-PLS.

papers.title_en: Holography and the Quantum Nature of Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: Black holes pose a lot of unsolved problems surrounding their fundamental properties. One of those puzzles is the black hole entropy problem. It has been known for a long time that black holes behave as thermodynamic systems and possess an entropy, but the question remains which microstates are responsible for this entropy. A theory of quantum gravity is needed to tackle this problem, currently the most viable example of which is string theory. The work of Strominger and Vafa, where they studied a class of asymptotically flat black holes, proves that string theory is indeed rich enough to account for the microstates responsible for the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. Recently, the focus has shifted to asymptotically AdS black holes after the discovery of the AdS/CFT correspondence.Holographic dualities, the first example of which was discovered by Maldacena, have proven to be highly successful in providing a microstate counting for the entropy of black holes. The black hole is constructed on the gravity side of the correspondence, and the dual field theory counts its states. In this thesis we study black holes in AdS5 and their dual 4d N=1 SCFTs. The general procedure can be summarized as follows. On the field theory side, supersymmetric states are counted using the superconformal index. From the index we can obtain the entropy via a Legendre transform. By requiring that the entropy is real, we obtain a prediction for the existence of a dual black hole with that same entropy. In the dual supergravity theory we look for such solutions and compute the Euclidean on-shell action to match to the index, and the horizon area to match to the CFT entropy.This procedure was successfully applied to the minimal sector of any AdS5/CFT4 duality by Cabo-Bizet, Cassani, Martelli and Murthy, to leading order in the large N expansion. Here we aim to move beyond these results by adding flavour symmetries to the problem and by going beyond leading order at large N. On the field theory side of the duality, we study the index and entropy of flavoured SCFTs. We observe that for some theories, the simple procedure for taking the Legendre transform in the literature can no longer be applied. In all previously known examples, the index satisfies a cubic identity which leads to a simple way of deriving the entropy. We show that this identity no longer holds for certain theories but can be replaced by a sixth order identity, resulting in a different, more complicated expression for the entropy. These results suggest the existence of a new class of dual black hole solutions to match this entropy with their horizon area.We then proceed to finding these new solutions. This is a highly nontrivial problem because the dual supergravity theories contain hypermultiplet scalars. We specifically choose to work in the duality derived from M5-branes wrapping around a Riemann surface, between a family of non-Lagrangian class S SCFTs and a set of N=2 supergravities with two vector multiplets and one hypermultiplet, both parametrized by a rational number z. For z=±1, the cubic identity is satisfied and the entropy takes the familiar, simple form. Here we can easily identify the dual black holes through a relation to the five-dimensional STU model. For other values of z, we need the sixth order identity and we must include the hypermultiplet scalars in the black hole solution. To simplify the problem, we look for the near-horizon extremal geometry and restrict to two equal angular momenta. We start from the known solution for z=1 and perform an expansion around this point. We find an analytical solution to first order in the expansion. Since we only solve in the near-horizon region, we lose access to the on-shell action and chemical potentials but can still compute the charges and the entropy. The entropy through the area law matches precisely with the field theory prediction. We therefore prove that these partial solutions are the first step towards identifying the new class of black hole solutions with non-zero hypermultiplet scalars.In the final part of this thesis we move beyond the leading order at large N and add higher-derivative corrections. We focus on the universal case where only the R-symmetry is turned on. In this case, the higher-derivative action including four derivatives can be fully determined up to two constants, which can be related to the conformal anomalies of the dual field theory using the holographic map. We then set out to confirm the first subleading corrections to the index and entropy from the gravity side of the duality. We argue that the corrections to the black hole solution are not needed for the Euclidean on-shell action. It suffices to substitute the leading order solution in the corrected action. We perform this calculation carefully and obtain a precise match with the superconformal index. For the entropy, the corrections to the solution are needed. Here we opt to compute the entropy from the quantum statistical relation and the first law. Finally, we comment on higher-derivative corrections to flavoured theories.

papers.title_en: <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> spectroscopy using <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>13</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>(<math><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></math>) resonant elastic scattering
papers.abstract_en: The detailed excitation functions for <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>13</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> elastic scattering and the additional thick target inverse kinematics measurements were analyzed using the <math><mi>R</mi></math> matrix approach. The analysis covered the excitation region in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> from 8.6 up to 11.2 MeV. Information on single particle widths of the levels in the <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus and shell model calculations are in good agreement. A comparative analysis of the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-cluster structures of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nuclei indicates their common underlying nature. However, the structure in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is more complex. In particular, each <math><mi>α</mi></math>-cluster level with spin <math><mi>J</mi></math> in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math> corresponds to several levels with spins <math><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. Unexpectedly, the reduced-width-weighted centroids of the higher-spin members of these doublets always lie at lower excitation energies in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>17</mn></mmultiscripts></math>.

papers.title_en: Investigating two-body cluster structures of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math>
papers.abstract_en: Two-body breakup mechanisms of the weakly bound nucleus <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math> were investigated through an exclusive coincidence measurement in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>197</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> system at a beam energy of 57 MeV. Coincident detection of two outgoing charged particles by an array of Si strip detector telescopes shows that the dominant two-body projectile breakup channels are <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Li</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>9</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>. Projectile excitation energies, reconstructed from the kinetic energies of the fragments, are found to reproduce the energies of specific excited states of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and thereby confirm the coexistence of both <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Li</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts><mtext>-</mtext><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>9</mn></mmultiscripts><mtext>-</mtext><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> two-body cluster configurations for <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>10</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. Continuum discretized coupled channels (CDCC) calculations, considering each of the above two cluster configurations separately, were able to explain the experimental cross sections for both breakup as well as elastic scattering simultaneously.

papers.title_en: Experimental study of the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>5</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction at 52 MeV: Probing the single-neutron wave function of the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts></math> ground state
papers.abstract_en: New experimental data for the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>5</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> one-neutron pickup reaction at 52 MeV were measured in inverse kinematics at the ACCULINNA-2 isotope in-flight separator at the Flerov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions, Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Dubna. The data were analyzed using two standard direct reaction models, the distorted wave Born approximation (DWBA) and coupled reaction channels. Single neutron wave functions for the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>6</mn></mmultiscripts></math> ground state obtained using three different nuclear structure methods, including the new cluster channel orthogonal function method, were tested and the dependence of the results of the reaction calculations on the properties of these wave functions was observed. The data were well reproduced by a DWBA calculation with the wave function obtained using the ab initio variational Monte Carlo method with no adjustable parameters.

papers.title_en: Possible coexistence of pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation in triaxial nuclei
papers.abstract_en: It has been conventionally assumed that triaxial deformation breaks the degeneracy of pseudospin doublets, leading to less discussion of pseudospin partner bands in triaxial nuclei. However, by considering the pairing correlations, the quasiparticle states of pseudospin doublets are found to remain nearly degenerate at appropriate Fermi energies in triaxial systems. In this work, we systematically investigate the pseudospin partner bands based on the <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> configuration in triaxial nuclei using the particle rotor model. For the first time, we propose the possible coexistence of pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation. Further analysis of angular momentum geometry and wave function components supports the identification of one structure as a pseudospin partner band and the other as a wobbling band. This study reveals a novel coexistence mode between pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation, illustrating the diversity of rotational excitations in atomic nuclei.

papers.title_en: Structure and decay of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-condensate candidates from cluster effective field theory interactions
papers.abstract_en: Dilute gas-like configurations of <math><mi>α</mi></math> particles, often termed <math><mi>α</mi></math> condensates, have been proposed to exist in certain excited states of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-conjugate nuclei. This work investigates the structural and decay properties of <math><mi>α</mi></math>-condensate candidates within a few-body framework using leading-order cluster effective field theory interactions. To isolate dilute <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> configurations, a constrained model space strategy is implemented inspired by Yamada and Schuck [Phys. Rev. C 69, 024309 (2004)], which constructs a description specifically for suprathreshold states. By explicitly decoupling the nonuniversal, compact configurations lying below the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> threshold, this framework describes <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> condensates as quasibound states localized within the Coulomb barrier. The stochastic variational method is used to perform theoretical calculations for the proposed <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow></math> condensates ranging from <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Be</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>8</mn></mmultiscripts></math> to <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ne</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>20</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The results not only map the formation of these novel cluster states in heavier <math><mi>α</mi></math>-conjugate nuclei but also offer critical insights into the applicability of few-body universality to charged particles.

papers.title_en: Critical response and enhanced parameter sensitivity in gapless fermionic systems
papers.abstract_en: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) quantifies the infinitesimal distance between two quantum states and characterizes the ultimate precision limit for the estimation of a parameter. While critical enhancement of QFI is well understood in gapped systems, its behavior in gapless topological phases remains less explored. In this work, we establish a general scaling criterion governing the emergence of singular many-body QFI in gapless fermionic systems. We show that, although single-particle QFI generically diverges near band-closing points when a control parameter shifts the position of the node, whether this divergence survives at the many-body level is determined by the codimension of the gapless manifold. Specifically, we demonstrate that in three-dimensional systems, the many-body QFI density diverges only when the codimension is less than or equal to two. This result leads to a sharp metrological distinction between Weyl semimetals and nodal-line semimetals. Furthermore, we construct explicit measurement protocols that saturate the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, showing that the predicted enhancement is, in principle, accessible via mode-resolved measurements. These results establish a direct connection among band topology, quantum geometry, and quantum metrology.

papers.title_en: Imaginarity-assisted minimum error discrimination
papers.abstract_en: Minimum error discrimination is a general approach for quantum-state discrimination. This work establishes a connection between quantum imaginarity and minimum error discrimination, investigating the conditions under which auxiliary quantum states can enhance the maximum average success probability (MASP) with real positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) or even achieve the MASP attainable with general POVMs. We prove that an auxiliary quantum state is nonreal if and only if it can enhance the MASP attainable with real POVMs in the composite system for at least one discrimination task. In particular, for pure states, only auxiliary maximally imaginary states can achieve the unrestricted MASP for all discrimination tasks. For a fixed ensemble, the assisted advantage is a convex, strongly monotonic imaginarity quantifier, but it need not be faithful. We characterize the ensembles for which it is faithful through a one-parameter family of discrimination problems and derive a spectral criterion for binary ensembles. These results identify when assisted discrimination efficiency defines a faithful imaginarity measure and clarify the operational role of imaginarity under real measurement constraints.

papers.title_en: Maximum confidence channel discrimination: Probe design, entanglement assistance, and sequential measurement
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we study maximum confidence measurement for quantum channel discrimination and develop optimization-based algorithms for designing both the probe state and measurement operators. We show that entanglement-assisted strategies with pure probe states and bounded reference dimensions suffice to achieve optimal performance. We characterize the optimal probe as a weakly Pareto optimal point of the achievable confidence region, and illustrate the framework on complementary dephasing qubit channels for which this region, the minimax probe, and the sequential design are obtained in closed form. Finally, we extend the framework to sequential maximum confidence measurements, where multiple observers perform measurements sequentially while maintaining the same confidence guarantees.

papers.title_en: Transport simulations with a constrained momentum-dependent chiral mean-field equation of state at various isospin fractions
papers.abstract_en: We present a comparison of the ultrarelativistic quantum molecular dynamics model using a chiral mean field (CMF) equation of state with flow and pion production data in heavy ion collisions at low beam energies <math><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>lab</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>2.0</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> GeV and varying isospin fraction. The CMF model parameters are constrained by known properties of the high density equation of state of quantum chromodynamics at varying isospin fractions. This allows us to calculate the equation of state as well as nuclear interactions for different physical systems like neutron stars and heavy ion collisions in a consistent way. It is found that heavy ion reactions at the upcoming FAIR facility will only have marginal sensitivity on the isospin dependence of the high-density equation of state. At lower beam energies, comparing to FOPI, HADES, and <math><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>π</mi><mtext>RIT</mtext></mrow></math> data, the sensitivity is higher but the observed deviations and systematic uncertainties of the existing data are larger than the sensitivity to the symmetry energy.

papers.title_en: Incorporating Heightened Scrutiny into a Large HEP Software Project
papers.abstract_en: In 2023, DUNE began re-evaluating the requirements of its data-processing framework, which led to commissioning a new design that would better fit neutrino physics than the existing reconstruction frameworks designed for collider physics. Due to the radical changes expected, significant multi-institutional effort has been directed toward the creation of the Phlex framework. In addition, the tight timelines in which to implement such a framework have invited scrutiny from various parties, including DUNE itself, the host laboratory Fermilab, and the US Department of Energy. After briefly discussing the unique needs of neutrino physics, we will recount how the Phlex development team has approached the design and development of a framework in the context of this heightened scrutiny. This process began with a systems-engineering approach to formally manage the requirements DUNE has of its framework. What followed was, for the first time in the HEP community, a review of the framework’s conceptual design by a panel of external framework experts before developers proceeded to the implementation. The implementation efforts have led to a series of prototypes that are being used to provide rapid feedback from Phlex users to framework developers. We will discuss how each of these steps has resulted in a strong design that has the backing of the DUNE experiment, Fermilab, and the US Department of Energy.

papers.title_en: Modified gravity models for inflation with non-minimal coupling trace of energy-momentum tensor of the scalar field and Gauss-Bonnet invariant
The Changing Meaning of One-Loop Exactness in $\mathcal{N}=2$ Supersymmetric Yang--Mills Theory
papers.abstract_en:
One of the striking achievements of supersymmetric field theory was to
recast difficult perturbative statements in increasingly compact
structures governed by symmetry, analyticity, holomorphy, and geometry.
In four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory, the phrase
``one-loop exact'' records this development especially clearly.  This
survey reconstructs the quantum-field-theoretic statements compressed
into that phrase.  Early multiloop calculations and supergraph/background-field methods established an ultraviolet theorem about higher-loop
gauge-coupling counterterms.  Work on $\mathcal{N}=2$ quantization, dimensional
reduction, and invariant regulators then exposed the prescriptions needed
to realize that theorem in perturbation theory.  Anomaly and holomorphy
arguments reorganized the protected information in terms of distinguished
Wilsonian couplings, while Seiberg's 1988 formulation connected it to
non-perturbative physics.  In Seiberg--Witten theory the same slogan came
to describe the perturbative truncation of the Coulomb-branch
prepotential, whose exact form nevertheless contains instanton
corrections.  We distinguish holomorphic Wilsonian, canonically normalized,
1PI, and Coulomb-branch couplings and show explicitly why finite scheme
changes delimit all-orders beta-function statements.  The pre-Seiberg
origin of the non-renormalization theorem is well preserved in specialist
literature; priority revision is therefore not the main claim.  Rather,
the history is treated as a sequence of translations from ultraviolet
renormalization to holomorphic low-energy geometry.  Recovering the QFT
vocabulary of counterterms, regulators, Ward identities, prescriptions,
and effective actions identifies the physical content that the later,
more economical language encodes.

papers.title_en: Geodesic motion in quadratic gravity spacetimes
Phenomenology of Glueballs in Effective Hadronic Models
New Analytic Methods in Black Hole Perturbation Theory
papers.abstract_en:
Motivated by the steady developments in gravitational-wave astronomy, this dis-
sertation focuses on the analytical aspects of black hole perturbation theory. We
present novel analytical techniques that deal with quasinormal modes (QNMs)
and scattering amplitudes of black holes.
Like a string or a bell, black holes tend to vibrate at the lowest possible frequency
or the fundamental frequency. These fundamental frequencies are known numer-
ically, but the analytic description or the mathematical tools necessary for their
understanding are not fully developed. In the first part of the dissertation, we
present one such tool, which utilizes the connection between equations describing
small perturbations of ordinary black holes and Seiberg-Witten theory.
In the next part, we investigate the vibrations of black holes embedded in four-
dimensional spacetime with negative or positive cosmological constant. In the
case of the negative cosmological constant, the Seiberg-Witten approach proves
to be more complicated to implement, and we propose an alternative method to set up perturbation theory for both small and large black holes in an analytical
manner. We reveal a new underlying recursive structure that involves multiple
polylogarithms.
In the final part of the dissertation, we introduce a novel approach to black
hole scattering amplitudes based on a new set of special functions called multiple
polyexponential integrals. By solving the Regge-Wheeler equation perturbatively
in the small-frequency regime, we determine the monodromy in the near-spatial
infinity region and derive a specific partial diﬀerential equation on the elements
of the scattering matrix. As a result, we pinpoint the exact form of scattering
amplitudes in Schwarzschild spacetime.

papers.title_en: Exact Methods for Spectral Problems via Conformal Field Theory, Supersymmetric Gauge Theory, and Topological Strings
papers.abstract_en:
In this thesis, we develop and apply methods inspired by two-dimensional conformal field
theory, supersymmetric gauge theory, and topological string theory to the study of spectral
problems. In the first part, we investigate periodic spectral problems governed by the
Lamé and Heun equations, including confluent limits of the latter. These equations arise
both as classical limits of BPZ equations satisfied by degenerate Virasoro conformal blocks
and as quantized Seiberg–Witten curves of four-dimensional N = 2 SU(2) gauge theories.
The two descriptions are related by the AGT correspondence, under which degenerate
classical conformal blocks are mapped to surface-defect partition functions in the Nekrasov–
Shatashvili (NS) limit. We solve the connection problem for the Lamé equation and develop
a systematic resummation procedure, based on suitable limits of blow-up equations, for bulk
and defect NS functions. The resummation resolves their singular instanton expansions at
resonant values of the Floquet exponent and reveals the branch structure of the accessory
parameters and Floquet solutions, whose branch points determine the edges of spectral
bands and gaps. For the Lamé equation, the resonant limit of the resummed accessory
parameter agrees with the values obtained independently from isomonodromic and orbifolddefect
constructions. The latter also provides the corresponding (anti-)periodic solutions.
For the Heun equation, we extend the resummation procedure to include the Floquet
solutions, obtaining at resonance both the accessory parameters and the corresponding
(anti-)periodic solutions. We further construct their logarithmic companions and analyze
the resonant monodromy, distinguishing the mass loci where spectral gaps close from the
smaller loci where the resonant monodromy becomes semisimple.
In the second part, we study finite-difference equations obtained by quantizing the mirror
curves of the Y N,0 geometries, which engineer five-dimensional N = 1 SU(N) gauge theories.
In the framework of the open topological string/spectral theory (TS/ST) correspondence,
we construct exact generalized eigenfunctions that are expected to be entire in the open
and closed moduli and to become square-integrable when the spectral moduli belong
to the appropriate exact quantization locus. Their four-dimensional limit gives explicit
analytic solutions to the eigenvalue problem associated with HN = 2ΛN cosh(p) + VN(x),
where VN(x) is an arbitrary monic polynomial of degree N. These operators are solvable
finite-difference deformations of the Schrödinger Hamiltonians p2+VN(x), and our solutions
describe both bound states and resonances. We also identify special loci at which the
eigenfunctions exhibit enhanced decay. For confining potentials, this enhancement leads
to spectral degeneracies, while for potentials unbounded from below, it produces squareintegrable
states with real energies. We finally discuss the related operators with a sinh(p)
kinetic term, an inverted potential −VN(x), or both.

papers.title_en: The role of emergence in the swampland program
Polylogarithmic structure of Bragg diffraction in finite-coherence lattices
papers.abstract_en: We develop a polylogarithmic structure for Bragg diffraction based on a weighted multi-plane interference model. Within this kind of construction, the scattering amplitude is expressed as a polylogarithmic generating function. By introducing extra contributions with power-law and the usual exponential decay, it takes the form $F(q) = \textrm{Li}_m\left( e^{i qd - \epsilon }\right) $, where $\epsilon $ is a finite coherence length. In the infinite-coherence limit, Bragg enhancement is associated with the approach of the polylogarithmic argument to its boundary singular point $z=1$. This formulation provides a compact analytical framework for describing diffraction line shapes within a generalized correlation model in which peak positions, widths, and line shapes arise from a single analytic structure. Although we are able to recover the standard Bragg law for ideal crystals, the polylogarithm model captures deviations due to finite correlation length, disorder and non-uniform lattice coherence. We show that if Bragg peaks correspond to boundary singularities of the polylogarithm, a connection between diffraction theory and complex analysis arises. The proposed theoretical model may be particularly relevant for disordered or partially coherent materials, where conventional diffraction models often require additional phenomenological broadening assumptions.[graphic not available: see fulltext] ,[graphic not available: see fulltext]

papers.title_en: Improved classical optimization of fermionic Hamiltonians beyond Gaussian states
papers.abstract_en: We give a polynomial-time randomized classical algorithm that approximates the largest eigenvalue $λ_{\max}$ of a traceless quartic fermionic Hamiltonian $H$ on $n$ modes. The algorithm achieves energy at least $λ_{\max}/O(\sqrt n)$ and outputs either a fermionic Gaussian state or a polynomially sparse state in the Fock basis. This is achieved through a new upper bound on $λ_{\max}$ in terms of the maximum energy of a Gaussian state and $\sqrt{2^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}(H^2)}$.

papers.title_en: Block encoding of semiseparable matrices via their generators
papers.abstract_en: We present an explicit quantum circuit that constructs a block encoding of a generator-representable semiseparable (one-pair) matrix directly from its two generators. For an $N\times N$ semiseparable matrix with $N=2^{n}$, the circuit uses $2n+2$ ancilla qubits and has $O({\rm polylog} N)$ depth, and it realizes a $(2\sqrt{N},\,2n+2,\,2 \sqrt{2}\ \varepsilon)$-block encoding, where $\varepsilon$ is controlled by the accuracy of the state-preparation routines that load the generators. The building blocks of the circuit are cyclic shifts, swaps, and Hadamard gates, each admitting an efficient implementation through the binary decomposition of the relevant indices.

papers.title_en: Verifiable Sampling for Delegated Generative Quantum Machine Learning
papers.abstract_en: Generative machine learning has shown remarkable results across a wide range of interdisciplinary tasks, motivating significant efforts toward Quantum Generative Models as a path to beyond-classical performance, given their capability of generating classically intractable distributions. However, comparatively little attention has been paid to securely delegating such computations to a powerful remote quantum server. In this work, we propose a blind and verifiable protocol for sampling that can be used for the inference phase of such quantum models. Such a protocol inherits blindness from Universal Blind Quantum Computing and achieves verifiability by exploiting known approaches based on trapification schemes. Alongside, to delegate the training phase, we discuss an extension of the previously proposed verifiable end-to-end Delegated Variational Quantum Algorithms (Inajetovic et al., Phys. Rev. Research, 2026). Beyond the usual Accept/Abort outcome characterizing verification protocols, the sampling protocol for inference also provides, even against a malicious server, an estimation of the amount of corrupted generated samples, i.e., a fine-grained feature describing the quality of the outcome connecting verification protocols and application-level benchmarking.

papers.title_en: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
papers.abstract_en: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.

papers.title_en: Global Optimization of Beam Profiles for Suppressing the Bump-On-Tail Instability
papers.abstract_en: A particle beam with constant intensity that propagates into a plasma triggers a bump-on-tail instability.
